newsitem.title: FRANCE: UAP may sell much of Scor stake.
newsitem.headline: UAP may sell much of Scor stake.

text.p: French insurer UAP said on Friday it could dispose of a large portion of its 41 percent stake in leading French reinsurer Scor when Scor is listed on the New York Stock Exchange this autumn.
A spokesman for Union des Assurances de Paris, Scor's largest shareholder, said the disposal could be "significant" but would depend on market conditions.

UAP's comments came after fellow French insurers Assurances Generales de France (AGF) and Axa announced they had disposed of their stakes in Scor over the last few months, a move flagged earlier by the companies.
Industry sources said the shares had been sold into the market and that one buyer had been a German investment fund.

UAP chairman Jacques Friedmann said in June the insurer did not consider its Scor holding to be a strategic asset and that it could cut it at the time of Scor's New York listing, expected in late September. The shares are listed in UAP's books at about 195 francs, a source close to the company said.

AGF said it had sold 9.0 percent of its 9.71 percent stake Scor, making a 47 million franc net capital gain. Axa sold its full 9.7 percent stake for a net capital gain of 22.5 million francs. Part of AGF's stake went to Societe Suisse which bought 2.25 percent of the French reinsurer in July.
Shares in Scor have climbed by more than 33 percent since the start of the year, making conditions ripe for disposal. They closed up two francs at 206 on Friday.

The rise is due partly to takeover speculation spurred by a consolidation wave sweeping the global reinsurance sector. Some analysts say Scor could be a target for a large U.S. reinsurer seeking a window on Europe, but others said the share was just undervalued.
The French government founded Scor in 1970 to give France a reinsurer of international standing.
